questions.question:

Panacea
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

• The word **"panacea"** means a solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases. (सर्वरोगहारी औषधि)
 
 
• **Example: **Some people believe that technology is a panacea for all problems facing humanity.
 
 
 
• **"Remedy" **refers to a medicine or treatment for a disease or injury, or a means of counteracting or eliminating something undesirable. (उपाय)
 
 
• **Example: **The doctor prescribed a remedy for the patient's chronic headaches.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

• **Survey **(सर्वेक्षण): A general view, examination, or description of someone or something.
 
 
• **Example:** The company conducted a survey to understand customer satisfaction.
 
 
 
• **Pressure **(दबाव): Continuous physical force exerted on or against an object by something in contact with it.
 
 
• **Example: **The pressure of the water against the dam was immense.
 
 
 
• **Miracle **(चमत्कार): An extraordinary and welcome event that is not explicable by natural or scientific laws and is therefore attributed to a divine agency.
 
 
• **Example:** The recovery of the patient was nothing short of a miracle.

questions.question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

Everyone says that waking up early in the morning is beneficial for our health and overall well-being. But it is__ easier said than done.__

options.text: to start performing better than before
not as easy as it seems to be

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"easier said than done"** means something that is not as easy as it seems to be. (कहना आसान है करना मुश्किल)

 
 
• **Example:** Quitting smoking is easier said than done; many people struggle to give up the habit.
 
 
 
• **"Not as easy as it seems to be"** means something that appears simple but is actually difficult to achieve or accomplish. (जितना आसान लगता है उतना नहीं है)
 
 
• **Example:** Losing weight might seem straightforward, but it is not as easy as it seems to be.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: A life filled with excitement** (रोमांच से भरी जिंदगी): Refers to a lifestyle that is full of thrilling and adventurous experiences.

 
 
• **Example:** He dreams of a life filled with excitement, traveling around the world and experiencing new cultures.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: A step towards better health** (बेहतर स्वास्थ्य की ओर एक कदम): Refers to an action taken to improve one's health.
 
 
• **Example:** Incorporating a balanced diet and regular exercise is a step towards better health.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To start performing better than before** (पहले से बेहतर प्रदर्शन करने लगना): Refers to improving one's performance compared to previous attempts.
 
 
• **Example:** After months of practice, he started performing better than before in his piano recitals.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

While she / was watched / the movie, / her phone rang.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. was watched .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the past continuous tense, describing an action that was happening when another action occurred.
 
• In past continuous tense, the correct structure is **"was/were + present participle (verb+ing)".**
 
• The segment **"was watched"** is incorrect because **"watched" is** the past tense form of the verb and does not fit the continuous tense structure.
 
• The correct form should be "was watching". Therefore, the segment "was watched" contains the grammatical error.

Correct sentence: *While she was watching the movie, her phone rang.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Past Continuous Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + was/were + verb (base form + ing)
 
• **Example:** He was playing when it started to rain.
 
• **Usage:** Describes an ongoing action in the past that was interrupted by another action.
 
 
 
• **Present Participle (verb+ing):** The form of the verb used to indicate continuous action.

__
 
• The passage discusses the concept of phobia and differentiates it from a regular fear.
 
• Fear is being described generally here, making the article "a" appropriate to refer to it as a singular, non-specific instance.
 
• Other options ("**one**," "**those**," and "**these**") do not fit the context of referring to fear as a general, non-specific notion.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *A phobia is an irrational fear of an object, situation or living thing. While fear is (1) a__ natural response to danger, phobias often occur (2) __in__ response to something unlikely to cause real harm. In some cases, a person with a (3) __phobia__ will meet the diagnostic criteria for a specific phobia, which is a type of anxiety disorder. Someone with a specific phobia will (4) __experience__ intense fear and anxiety when confronted with the source of the phobia, which could include blood, heights or specific animals like dogs. Phobias are (5) __marked__ by significant distress and often cause a person to avoid the source of their fear or suffer from extreme anxiety when faced with it. Someone experiencing a phobia that is interfering with everyday life should consider undergoing treatment for their phobia, as outcomes for professional care are typically favourable.*
